diagnostic_evidence.quote: It follows that $\mathcal{K}g=zg$ and hence $z$ is an eigenvalue.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing r=(\mathcal K_F-\lambda I)g gives \(\mathcal K_F^n g-\lambda^n g=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\lambda^j\mathcal K_F^{n-1-j}r\), whose bound generally contains powers of \(\max\{\|\mathcal K_F\|,|\lambda|\}\). The paper itself constructs Koopman eigenvalues \(\mu\) with \(|\mu|>1\). Taking a normalized \(\mu\)-eigenfunction and \(\lambda\) within \(\epsilon\) of \(\mu\) yields error \(|\mu^n-\lambda^n|\), which grows like \(n\epsilon |\mu|^{n-1}\), not \(O(n\epsilon)\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed estimate by the telescoping-sum bound involving powers of \(\|\mathcal K_F\|\) and \(|\lambda|\), and state the linear-in-n estimate only under suitable contraction assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed long-time physical coherence of general pseudoeigenfunctions is unsupported; outside contraction-like regimes, the error may grow exponentially.
issues.title: Pseudoeigenfunction error need not grow only linearly in time
issues.why_classification: The correction is local but materially weakens the asserted time-growth rate over the paper's general non-measure-preserving setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We assume that the map $F$ is nonsingular with respect to $\omega$, meaning that
$$
\omega(E)=0\quad \text{implies that}\quad \omega(\{x:F(x)\in E\})=0.
$$
This ensures that the Koopman operator is well-defined
We assume that $\mathcal{K}$ is a bounded linear operator on the Hilbert space $L^2(\mathcal{X},\omega)$.
\Omega_{\mathcal{X}}&=\left\{F:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{X}\text{ such that $F$ is continuous and non-singular, $\mathcal{K}_F$ is bounded}\right\},

issues.failure_explanation: The main-text class quantifies over every continuous self-map, while the paper's own functional-analytic setup requires nonsingularity for composition to be well-defined on L2 equivalence classes and boundedness for the asserted compact spectral problem. For example, a constant map on an interval with Lebesgue measure is continuous but sends the whole interval into a null singleton, so composition depends on the representative of an L2 class. The appendix silently proves only the restricted theorem with nonsingularity and boundedness.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the main-text classes to nonsingular maps inducing bounded Koopman operators, as in the appendix, and correspondingly withdraw the claim that the theorem covers arbitrary continuous systems.
issues.overall_effect: The two-limit assertion for \(\Omega_{\mathcal X}^{\alpha}\) and the advertised three-limit result for all continuous systems include inputs for which their target spectral set is not defined in the stated framework.
issues.title: Theorem 2 includes continuous maps for which the Koopman operator is undefined or unbounded
issues.why_classification: The available repair excludes an advertised general regime and changes the central quantifier of the theorem rather than merely filling a local proof detail.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $F\in\Omega_p$ be the skew product map
$
F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x)),
$
An eigenfunction $g\in\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$ is non-trivial. A system is weakly mixing precisely when there are no non-trivial eigenfunctions.
In the above construction, we switched between $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=0$ for $k$ odd and $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=1$ for $k$ even.

issues.failure_explanation: Every function of x alone is invariant under this skew product: for \(g(x,y)=h(x)\), \(\mathcal K_Fg=g\). Choosing any nonzero mean-zero h gives an eigenfunction with eigenvalue 1 in \(\mathrm{span}\{1\}^{\perp}\), regardless of whether f is strictly increasing. Thus part (a) of the lemma is false, and the lower-bound proof cannot alternate between absence and presence of nontrivial eigenfunctions as claimed.

failure_location.quote: If $f$ is strictly increasing on $[-\pi,0]$, the spectral measure of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with respect to any $g\in L^2(\mathcal{X},\omega)$ is continuous on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$. It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the skew-product family by systems without a nonconstant invariant base factor and re-establish the required smooth phase transition while preserving all sampling and Lipschitz constraints.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed one-limit impossibility and optimal two-limit classification for deciding existence of nontrivial eigenfunctions are not established by the supplied construction. The proof of the accompanying pure-point-spectrum lower bound also invokes the false lemma and therefore needs a separate valid spectral argument.
issues.title: The skew products used for the eigenfunction lower bound always have nonconstant invariant eigenfunctions
issues.why_classification: The counterexample defeats the central phase-transition mechanism, and repairing it requires a fundamentally different adversarial dynamical construction rather than a local amendment.
